changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6310-designer-formula-key-retired.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `designer.field.formula` (`'Formula (CEL)'`) in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, a different and live key belonging to metadata-admin's `ObjectFieldInspector` — the surface that still authors formula expressions.

### `.changeset/7125-dashboard-empty-state-keys-retired.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `table.noRows` (`'No rows to display'`) and `engine.form.noRows` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, read at `widgets.tsx`) — two different, same-named keys in different namespaces. Nor the comments in `WidgetEmptyState.tsx`, `DatasetWidget.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and `PivotTable.tsx` that record WHY three widgets with three strings became one shared empty state; the packs' own comment keeps that rationale and now names the retirement instead of a row that is gone.

### `.changeset/8632-malformed-picklist-option-loud.md`

- names `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Two new strings land in the designer's own `en` / `zh` tables — the metadata-admin console owns its strings in `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` and is deliberately outside the ten locale packs (`packages/i18n/README.md`, "Scope — the `engine.*` carve-out").

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `4aebea00a` (merge-base with origin/main): 8 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1634 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2223 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36355837886)

The one run: a throwaway `git worktree add --detach` at the head under the scratch dir, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` (6s, every `@object-ui/*` resolves to `src` through the root vitest aliases so no build was needed), the six component sources checked out at the base `4aebea00` (each worktree blob equal to the base blob: `e94d9e9aa1`, `df0f2f2218`, `3d0664759b`, `3b72e31939`, `2bcac48ca8`, `4b165dc5af`) with `i18n.ts` (`7711f1fe35`) and the pin file (`797aeaa0bc`) at the head, then `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=review-10857 os-verify-lock.sh -c 'timeout 540 pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/previewStrings.i18n-10848.test.tsx'` from the worktree root (AGENTS.md's repo-root spelling). VERDICT `command-exit 1 · held the lock 12s · waited 87s`. Result `Tests 10 failed | 10 passed (20)`: the ten failures are exactly the ten zh cases, every en control passed. Afterwards the worktree was restored (`git diff HEAD` 0 bytes) and removed with `git worktree remove` (no `--force`); `git worktree list` on the main checkout no longer lists it. No repo gate and no other suite was run.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The heading via a hook — RIGHT.**
- `PreviewErrorHeading` is a function component that reads `useMetadataLocale()` and renders `t('engine.previewShell.renderFailed', locale)`; the class boundary renders it in place of the literal. `useMetadataLocale` is `useObjectTranslation().language` collapsed to `'zh-CN'` or `'en-US'`.
- Every production host of a preview computes the `locale` prop it passes from the same hook in the same tree: `ResourceEditPage` (`const locale = useMetadataLocale();` then `locale={locale}` on the mounted `PreviewComponent`), `EmbeddedItemEditor` (same, on `Preview`), `StudioDesignSurface` (same, on `Preview` and on `StudioCanvas`; its `SourcePageEditor mode="preview"` mount sits in the same tree). So in the product the heading and the preview's own words are read from one source by construction; the 22 preview files with 25 boundary call sites need no prop.
- Where no provider exists: `useObjectTranslation` returns `language: context?.language || i18n.language || 'en'` and does not throw without an `I18nProvider` (react-i18next hands back an empty instance), so the heading reads the en row, "Preview failed to render", the same bytes as before. No test in the tree asserts that heading at all (`git grep "Preview failed to render"` over `*.test.*` is empty), so no provider-less test moved. In the console preview gallery, `I18nProvider` is mounted with `defaultLanguage: 'en'` while `?locale=` feeds only the typed `locale` prop, so there the heading follows the provider (en) and the preview body follows `?locale=`; the dev states this in the PR body. It is the same divergence the gallery already has for every hook-reading site.
- The hook is the family's source: `AddWidgetPicker` (objectui#10832, merged), `FlowExprIssue`, `ConditionBuilder`, `FlowObjectListField`, `FlowReferenceField`, `VariableTextInput`, `useFlowScope` all read `useMetadataLocale()`; triage `5859968829` names it as an accepted source.

**2. ScreenPreview — RIGHT.**
- `locale?: string` is optional; both homes pass it: `FlowNodeInspector` (destructures `locale` from `MetadataInspectorProps`; `locale={locale}` on `ScreenPreview`) and `FlowSimulatorPanel` (`locale` prop; `locale={locale}` on the paused screen; it already passed `locale` to `new FlowSimulator(nodes, edges, locale)`).
- Plural rows: en `hiddenOne` = `'{count} field hidden by its “visible when” condition.'`, `hiddenOther` = `'{count} fields hidden by their “visible when” conditions.'`; substituting 1 and 2 gives exactly what the base JSX rendered (`{hidden} field{hidden === 1 ? '' : 's'} hidden by {hidden === 1 ? 'its' : 'their'} “visible when”{' '}condition{hidden === 1 ? '' : 's'}.`), confirmed by the red run's diffs (`"1 field hidden by its “visible when” condition."`, `"2 fields hidden by their “visible when” conditions."`). zh rows are identical for one and other, `'有 {count} 个字段因其“显示条件”而隐藏。'`, which is correct for Chinese (no plural inflection); placeholders `{count}` on both sides.
- Every literal in the file: localized are the header, the empty state, Submit, the no-backend note (`noDataSourceMessage`), the hidden-field note. Deliberately literal: the interpolated `title` and `description` (author data), the field labels drawn by `ScreenView` (author data). `ScreenView`'s own defaults (`'Save & Continue'`, `'This step renders an object form but no data source is available.'`) never render here: the preview passes `showSubmit: false`, `showCancel: false`, and always passes `noDataSourceMessage`, which `ScreenView` reads with `??`. Nothing else in the file is English chrome.

**3. The CEL frames — RIGHT.**
- `evalValueEnvelope`, `evalGuard`, `evalBranchPredicate` and the private `evalCelPredicate` take an optional trailing `locale`, the shape `validateFlowDraft(nodes, edges, locale?)` already had. The producer text is verbatim: `tFormat('engine.flowSim.note.celEvaluationFailed', locale, { message: result.error.message })` and the `celConditionFailed` twin; the red run shows (the CEL source `discount ‹greater-than› 1`, its operator re-spelled here) `"discount ‹greater-than› 1: condition failed to evaluate as CEL: Unknown variable: discount"` on the base and the zh case expects `"discount ‹greater-than› 1: 条件无法按 CEL 求值:Unknown variable: discount"`, the producer's sentence unchanged and read from `@objectstack/formula` itself by `producerMessage`. The spec refusals (`structuralConditionRefusal`, `predicateSlotRefusal`, `EVALUATED_EXPRESSION_SOURCE_REQUIRED`, `ASSIGNMENT_VALUE_ENVELOPE_REFUSAL`, Zod issues joined with their path) are returned as they were.
- Other callers: `git grep` at the head finds the evaluators called only from `flow-simulator.ts`, at exactly the three sites that now pass `this.locale` (`evalBranchPredicate(cond.expression, this.state.variables, this.locale)`, `evalValueEnvelope(value, this.state.variables, this.locale)`, `evalGuard(e.condition, vars, this.locale)`); no test file calls them directly. `evalCelPredicate` is not exported. So no caller silently stays English.
- Reusing `engine.flowSim.note.evaluationFailed` (en `'Evaluation failed.'`, zh `'求值失败。'`): its one other use site is the simulator's out-edge pass, `g.kind === 'fault' ? g.error : this.say('engine.flowSim.note.evaluationFailed')`, the same sentence for the same meaning (an evaluation that failed with no more specific reason); the base `flow-sim-validate.ts` carried the identical literal three times, and all three catch sites now read the row. Meaning preserved at both sites.

**4. Rows — RIGHT.**
- `git diff 4aebea00..e386a59 -- i18n.ts`: 0 removed lines; 9 keys added, each exactly twice (once in `ENGINE_STRINGS_EN`, once in `ENGINE_STRINGS_ZH`): `engine.flowSim.note.celEvaluationFailed`, `engine.flowSim.note.celConditionFailed`, `engine.previewShell.renderFailed`, `engine.screenPreview.header`, `engine.screenPreview.empty`, `engine.screenPreview.submit`, `engine.screenPreview.noDataSource`, `engine.screenPreview.hiddenOne`, `engine.screenPreview.hiddenOther`.
- Byte for byte against the base sources: `'Preview failed to render'` (PreviewShell), `'Preview'`, `'Add a title, description, fields, or an object form to preview this screen.'`, `'Submit'`, `'Connect to a backend to preview this object form.'` (ScreenPreview), `'CEL evaluation failed: '` + message and `'condition failed to evaluate as CEL: '` + message (flow-sim-validate template literals) all equal their en rows; the two hidden rows equal the base JSX output for 1 and 2 as shown under item 2. Placeholders identical across en/zh for all nine (`{message}` ×2, `{count}` ×2, none ×5), checked programmatically.
- Gate semantics: `check-i18n-designer-table-parity.mjs` ("every `en` row has a `zh` row and every shared row carries the same `{placeholders}`") and the designer leg of `check-i18n-en-drift.mjs` ("the `en` value changed and `zh` did not", against the merge base) are both satisfied by inspection; both run in `ci.yml`'s `type-check` job, whose check-run "Type Check" is `success` on the head.

**5. Pins — RIGHT.**
